source_marillier.author: Leon Marillier
source_marillier.title: La place du totemisme dans l'evolution religieuse, a propos d'un livre recent (F. B. Jevons: An Introduction to the History of Religion)

claim_policy: Operational concordance only. No direct claim that Lovejoy read the printed 1897 article. Institutional continuity is supplied separately by Lovejoy's documented active participation in Marillier's 1898-99 EPHE conferences.

records.marillier_primary: Criticizes reduction of multiple forms of sacrifice to one original sacrifice of union/sacramental type; facts overflow narrow frames; allows parallel classes of distinct though analogous beliefs and practices.
records.marillier_location: RHR 36 (1897), second installment opening, beginning printed p.321
records.lovejoy_operation: Separates originally distinct sacrificial motives; syncretism can combine them later; ceremonial cannibalism, magical transfer, propitiation, funerary provision and communion are not collapsed into one type.

records.marillier_primary: An interpretation that does not explain the whole group may still be partially exact; corrects 'not the true reason' to 'not the only reason'.
records.marillier_location: RHR 36 (1897), funerary taboo discussion in second installment
records.lovejoy_operation: Tests multiple determinants or motives in one case instead of replacing one universal explanation with another.

records.marillier_primary: A heterogeneous set of interdictions should not be grouped as one explanatory class merely because of external resemblances; where one theory fails, seek other motives.
records.lovejoy_operation: Ritual killing is not automatically sacrifice; sacred animal is not automatically divinity/sacrifice; circumcision is not partial human sacrifice; ceremoniality does not prove sacramental cannibalism.

records.marillier_primary: Corpse transmits its defining property by simple contact; dangerous influence propagates; purification/preservation and isolation counter contagion.
records.lovejoy_operation: Moves from taboo/contact/blood to body-part and blood efficacy, charms, protective objects and transferable qualities.

records.marillier_primary: Taboo sacredness varies with mana, glossed as supernatural and magical force; superior mana can overcome an interdiction.
records.lovejoy_operation: Distinguishes direct action on natural forces, efficacy of blood/body parts, fetish through indwelling spirit, and intrinsic efficacy of charm/amulet/plant/stone.

records.marillier_primary: An animal may house a spirit, possess supernatural power and receive cult without therefore being a totem; the term should retain a limited and precise meaning.
records.lovejoy_operation: Maintains distinctions among sacrifice/ritual killing, cannibalism/communion, fetish/charm, blood use/union, initiation/sacrifice.
